   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Michael Atkins, BURY



Ron & Brian

I have read about Spectrums
being linked together and would
like to know what benefits this
provides. Can you please help me
with this?


Also, would there be anything to
be gained if I were to link my
+3 to a 48k Spectrum which has
been dormant for the last 5
years. If so, then how would I
go about connecting the two
machines and how would I get
them to communicate?


In reading through some back
issues of Outlet I have noticed
several letters from +3 owners
who cannot get BRIGHT to operate
on their monitors. If this has
not been resolved (I'm still
catching up on the back issues)
then I may be able to offer a
solution.


When I acquired my +3 in 1988 I
already had a Phillips TV/monit-
or (14CT2007/25S) and on phoning
Philips they put me in touch
with a firm called Adapt Electr-
onics. They supplied me with a
cable to connect the RGB socket
of the +3 to the CVBS socket of
the monitor. The wiring connect-
ions are as follows:-


  CVBS socket       RGB socket

    2 CVBS           1 green
    4 sound          2 sync
    3 ground         3 ground
    1,5,6 N.C.       4 red
                     5  blue
                     6  sound

I know that five years is a long
time in the computor world and
maybe Adapt Electronics are no
longer in business, however,just
in case, their address was:-


       20 Starling Close
         Buckhurst Hill
         Essex IG9 5TN
       (tel 01 504 2840)


Finally, regarding the use of
Masterfile to replace Outdex, I
think the +3 version will be
capable of holding a vast number
of records. I am just completing
a database of all the Outletters
from Issue 23 and have currently
got over 1,000 records on file
with over 10K of RAM space
available. If you think that
this file will be of sufficient
interest for including in the
Addenders then please let me
know. It will probably be up to
60K in size.

Keep up the good work.

        Michael Atkins

Brian Cavers to Michael Atkins

Yes, whenever any reader has a
program, article, or other soft-
ware and wonder if it is suit-
able for OUTLET, always send it
in with the question. We return
the disc anyway and often can't
make a judgement without seeing
the item in question. In any
event, it is less trouble to the
contributor in the long run and
only one stamp is needed!

In this case, I can't really
judge because you don't say what
information is included with the
file of OUTLETTERS. If it is a
simple list of readers' names
and the issue -  perhaps not; if
however, it has subject matter -
YES!!!! VERY USEFUL!

Computers can be connected if
they each have an RS232 socket,
a cable, and suitable software
in each computer to send and
receive software. If each had a
modem then the computers could
be in separate parts of the
world and the software could be
sent down a telephone line.


Within the same room or area
linked by a cable then there are
all sorts of possibilities. One
might edit a machine code pro-
gram on one machine and send it
straight to the other machine to
test. If it crashed then one can
immediately continue on the
first machine without having to
reload the assembler and files.


Text files or graphic art for
use on one type of machine might
be prepared on a superior word
processor or graphics program on
a second machine and transferred
later. It is even possible to
play a game with two people on
different computers each with
their own screen but in compet-
ition in the same game.

A machine might act as a slave
to another which could pass data
requiring time-consuming proc-
essing such as calculations or
printing for it to handle while
the master machine carries on
with something else. Multiple
machines of course are linked in
offices to pass data as well as
in schools between teacher and
pupils.

Your +3 has an RS232 socket but
your 48K won't have unless you
have say, Interface 1 connected.
Even then I don't think the two
RS232's are compatible. They are
supposed to be standardised but
there are variations!I recommend
you leave your 48K on the shelf!

Incidentally,I pass programs and
other files between a SAM, 48K
Spectrum with +D, 48K with Opus,
+3 and now even a PC all without
any RS232! Between the Spectrums
I go straight through a cassette
recorder, the +D can read SAM
Coupe discs(I am typing this on
OUTWRITE on a SAM); the Emulator
from BG SERVICES has a program
to transfer Spectrum program via
tape or +D disc!
                       Brian

         Miles Kinloch
            Flat 16,
       6 Drummond Street,
       Edinburgh EH8 9TU.

Dear Brian,

One area I haven't yet seen cov-
ered in any Spectrum publication
is a complete list of all +D and
Disciple port addresses and how
each one works. Is there perhaps
any chance of this subject being
covered in a future Drivechat?

Recently I considered buying a
Citizen 120D printer, but as a
cut-sheet user I found a problem
with the 'home' position of the
print-head being at the very
left.


Feeding in a single sheet with
the head in this position caused
the top of the paper at the
right-hand end to catch on the
vertical edges of the paper
guide ridges under the front
cover, i.e. where the paper
emerges. The paper needs to be
kept clear of these edges, and
the print-head is the only thing
which can ensure this.

I presume this is a point which
was perhaps overlooked when the
printer was designed. With my
present printer,a Brother M1109,
the home position of the head is
in the centre and this helps
keep the paper down equally at
each end when inserted, avoiding
any such problems.


How are the other popular 9-pin
printers designed in this
respect (e.g. Star LC10)? I have
never seen this point mentioned
in any reviews but it is import-
ant if you use only single
sheets.


Finally, speaking of printers,
does anyone know how to replace
the print head on a Brother
M1109? I know that some machines
are designed so that the user
can do this easily themselves
and give details in the manual.
The Brother M1109 manual makes
no mention of this, though, and
there is no obvious way (to me,
at least) how to detach the head
physically.


The reason I ask is because I
have just had the head replaced
by a local firm, who charged
over `70, although the head
itself was only `25 or so. I
have experience of electronics,
and if some one could tell me
how to go about it, then next
time it wears out I won't need
to pay someone else to do a job
I could perhaps easily do
myself. If anyone wants to write
to me, please feel free. [see
address at top of letter]

Meantime, all the best.

            Regards,

         Miles Kinloch

Brian Cavers to Miles Kinloch

My printer is the M1009. It too
snags single sheet paper! Its
manual DOES show how to change
the printer head but I somehow
doubt it is the same as your
M1109. I would have sent you a
photocopy anyway when I returned
your disc but it is difficult
for me to get a photocopy here
without being without my printer
manual for maybe a couple of
weeks and I really do need to
refer to it often. If you think
it might help though then let me
know and when an opportunity
comes up I will send you a copy.

Incidentally, even with the info
I found it a real Chinese puzzle
to extract!

We have received requests from
several readers for Disciple/+D
info and I have made a note to
see what can be done but it is
very difficult to get hold of
this information ourselves!

Disciple can be paged in and out
with IN 187 and OUT 187 and the
+D with 231. However, it is more
usual to use RST 8 which works
on both to page the ROM and then
use hook codes.Read DRIVECHAT in
this very issue for info!

If you want to directly access
the drives at low level then I
don't think I have such info in
my records. If you want to expl-
ore then try saving the ROM to
disc and load it to high memory
into a disassembler.    Brian

Brian Cavers to Ron Smith

There are two or three possible
ways of solving the pound sign
problem.Firstly, WORDMASTER does
not seem to cater for the pound
sign itself within the text.That
is, I can see no way to enter a
pound "`" as I have here and get
WORDMASTER to print it properly.
However, there are ways of using
a different character to repre-
sent it in the text...

1. Use a hash(#) (SYMBOL PLUS 3)
in text where a "`" is needed.If
it prints as a "#" then set your
printer's dipswitch(consult your
printer manual) to the English
character set. Naturally, this
means you can't print a "#"!


2. Define a graphic character to
represent the code 156. If you
look in your WORDMASTER manual
you will see you use the command
character >def 1 156. To insert
a "`" in your text you then use
GRAPHICS key then 1.An inverse 1
(white on black) is shown on
screen and should print as a"`".
I don't use WORDMASTER myself so
I am not familiar with it but I
am sure you must then resave the
program to make the change perm-
anent. Again, check the manual.

3. Define a control code that
you don't use as a "`", eg, if
you never use subscript then use
the CUSTOM option to alter it to
send a 156 then use the GRAPHICS
key to insert an inverse "s".


I must explain that you do not
need an ESC (27) with the 156.An
ASCII code is a single number to
represent a character, eg. SPACE
is 32 and "A" is 65. You only
need an ESC code when you send a
control code such as italics.

As mentioned before, the "#" can
be printed as a "#" or a "`"
depending on which character set
is switched on in the printer.It
can be switched by a dipswitch
but it can also be switched by a
sequence of control codes so you
could use CUSTOM to alter a
sequence (say ITALICS if you
don't use them) to switch to "#"
using 27,82,0 or to "`" with
27,82,3. Use GRAPHICS+I then "#"
or GRAPHICS+i then "#" in the
text.

You're spoilt for choice with so
many solutions! Now for the left
margin problem...

The normal left margin codes are
27,108,n where n is size of the
margin you want. You do not say
if your printer differs from
this so check your printer manu-
al if in doubt. Then check the
CUSTOM screen to see that the
same sequence appears there for
the margin codes. In the copy of
WORDMASTER that I have it has
got 13,27,108 for the codes and
this seems misleading as there
is only room for 3 codes so the
13 must be removed.

Please let me know how you get
on and if you need more help.
                           Brian

Following are random jottings on
a recent modification to my +3 I
have made. It works well with my
monitor.So far (3 weeks) nothing
has blown up or given burning
smells so I think it's success-
ful! See what you think. Maybe

 [N.B. images in the following
 text will not print out true
 so adjust with biro!  - BC]


SPECTRUM +3 with TTL Monitor...

The Spectrum +2 (grey model)
will drive a TTL monitor as it
has 5 volts peek to peek output
from the RGB socket.However, the
+3 and presumably the black +2a
have RGBN outputs at Peritel
levels i.e., volt peek to peek,
and will not drive a convention-
al TTL or Analogue monitor.

To modify the +3 (issue 2) to
enable suitable output at TTL
levels is quite easy if you have
some electronics experience and
the correct tools. Good eyesight
plus magnifying glass are help-
ful. You will need a micropoint
soldering iron and solder sucker
- artery forceps are also very
useful.

Remove the screws from the base
and side of the +3 noting their
locations. Lift up the keyboard
and gently detach the keyboard
ribbon cables and also the
indicator LED. Put the keyboard
away safely.

Mark the connections to the disc
drive with TIPPEX and remove the
disc drive,noting the screws,and
put the drive safely with the
keyboard.

Remove the screws  securing the
main PC board to the base. Now
would be a good time to clean
the expansion port etc. contacts
- an ink rubber or a jeweller's
glass brush are excellent.


Also consider adding an external
connection to the board to
enable direct output of sound
using the marked connections on
the PC board to which the +2a's
cassette must be connected - the
sound output from here is much
better than fromm the stereo
connection provided by Amstrad .
The input connection also is
useful.


Examine the PC board behind the
RGB socket - the components are
marked. Unsolder and remove R35,
R36, R37, R33, R31, R42 (all 150
ohm). Substitute 68 ohm 1/3 watt
resistors.This modification will
give 8 colours but no 'BRIGHT'.


The monitor requires separate
horizontal and vertical synch-
ronisation signals - link these
together in the monitor's 9-pin
'D' plug and drive the linked
connection with the composite
synch output from the +3.

The improvement over the usual
smeared low-resolution output on
a TV is most noticeable and
enables easy reading of OUTLET
ADDENDER files (which use a sort
of pseudo-italic character set!)

The provision of BRIGHT is a
little more difficult and may be
judged by some readers as not
worth the extra trouble but can
be achieved as follows...


On the back of the board, break
the fine PC connection between
R42 & R43. Remove R42 and insert
a signal diode in its place
>-  -[__]]- end to RGB socket.

Take a fine, insulated wire and
solder to -[__]]- (left end as
shown here -away from the band)
of the new diode.

Carefully solder the other end
of the wire to the banded end of
D28 -[[__]- on the board.

Remove R41 150 ohm and R34 470
ohm and interchange R41 now 470
ohm and R34 now 150 ohm.

BRIGHT now is available from the
No.3 pin on the RGB socket which
used to supply 'audio out'.

Be very careful to avoid making
any connections to pins 1 and  5
as for reasons best known by
Amstrad,they supply 12 volts DC.

Before putting into use, examine
all connections very carefully -
a blob of solder or fragment of
debris bridging a connection
could have very serious effects.

The monitor in use is an EGA
Electishome with both analogue
and TTL inputs and the +3 works
very well in either mode.

If anyone is desperate to con-
vert their +3 but have not got
the necessary tools etc.,I might
be persuaded for a nominal sum
(see address at head of letter).
                      Dave Wood.

Brian Cavers to All

A few issues ago I put in a
letter about bit testing from
BASIC. The example I gave was
really very specific and when I
came to do another similar test
I got stuck so I went back to
Chris and Paul Oliver and have
come up with the following
definitive test to see if a
specific bit is set or not:

X= INT((n/2!b)-2*INT((n/2!b)/2))

where...

 n is the value being tested
 b is the bit being tested
 ! is the upright arrow symbol
   (it won't print here!)
                        more...

To clarify... Any value n can be
represented in binary as noughts
and ones, e.g., 7 is 00000111.
Each 1 or 0 is a "bit". As well
as, or instead of, representing
a whole value, computers often
use a value to represent up to
eight different values - one for
each bit - although each value
can only be 0 or 1. It saves
memory where the information is
something simple like CAPS LOCK
which can only be ON (1) or OFF
(0). The eight bits are usually
numbered 7 to 0 from left to
right so to test say, the left
bit of PEEK 32768 you would LET
b=7 and n=PEEK 32768 in the
formula on the last page and X
would result in a 0 or 1. Thus
endeth the lesson.
                        Brian

Brian Cavers to Nigel Cattell

First, be assured you are not a
pain because one of the purposes
of OUTLET is to solve problems
or to publish them so others can
solve them!

I'm not quite sure what you mean
by "SYMBOL SHIFT KEY & 2" but I
guess your problem is that your
printer needs to use the ESC "*"
graphics codes rather than the
ESC "K","L" and "M". Also, there
is no line 9256 in TOPCAL but my
guess is you may mean line 9756
which is the one to select the
Kempston option. Whatever option
anybody uses, our graphics dump
can be modified to use ESC "*"
by ADDING the following line...


9753 POKE 55044,5 :POKE 55066,62
     POKE 55067,10:POKE 55068,0
     POKE 55069,0 :POKE 55157,42
     POKE 55158,0 :POKE 55159,0
     POKE 55160,1

This should work in most OUTLET
programs with our graphics dump,
including TOPCAL. If not, check
out line 9769 which will have a
USR followed by an address.This
is usually 55E3 (means 55000) so
the above POKES are +44, +66 etc
but if it were say 60000 then
adjust accordingly, eg. 60044,
60066 etc. However, mostly it is

SPECTRUM +3 with TTL Monitor...

The Spectrum +2 (grey model) will drive a TTL monitor as it has 5 volts peek to peek output from the RGB socket.However, the +3 and presumably the black +2a have RGBN outputs at Peritel levels i.e., volt peek to peek, and will not drive a convention- al TTL or Analogue monitor.

To modify the +3 (issue 2) to enable suitable output at TTL levels is quite easy if you have some electronics experience and the correct tools. Good eyesight plus magnifying glass are help- ful. You will need a micropoint soldering iron and solder sucker - artery forceps are also very useful.

Remove the screws from the base and side of the +3 noting their locations. Lift up the keyboard and gently detach the keyboard ribbon cables and also the indicator LED. Put the keyboard away safely.

Mark the connections to the disc drive with TIPPEX and remove the disc drive,noting the screws,and put the drive safely with the keyboard.

Remove the screws  securing the main PC board to the base. Now would be a good time to clean the expansion port etc. contacts - an ink rubber or a jeweller's glass brush are excellent.

Also consider adding an external connection to the board to enable direct output of sound using the marked connections on the PC board to which the +2a's cassette must be connected - the sound output from here is much better than fromm the stereo connection provided by Amstrad . The input connection also is useful.

Examine the PC board behind the RGB socket - the components are marked. Unsolder and remove R35, R36, R37, R33, R31, R42 (all 150 ohm). Substitute 68 ohm 1/3 watt resistors.This modification will give 8 colours but no 'BRIGHT'.

The monitor requires separate horizontal and vertical synch- ronisation signals - link these together in the monitor's 9-pin 'D' plug and drive the linked connection with the composite synch output from the +3.

The improvement over the usual smeared low-resolution output on a TV is most noticeable and enables easy reading of OUTLET ADDENDER files (which use a sort of pseudo-italic character set!)

The provision of BRIGHT is a little more difficult and may be judged by some readers as not worth the extra trouble but can be achieved as follows...

On the back of the board, break the fine PC connection between R42 & R43. Remove R42 and insert a signal diode in its place >-  -[__]]- end to RGB socket.

Take a fine, insulated wire and solder to -[__]]- (left end as shown here -away from the band) of the new diode.

Carefully solder the other end of the wire to the banded end of D28 -[[__]- on the board.

Remove R41 150 ohm and R34 470 ohm and interchange R41 now 470 ohm and R34 now 150 ohm.

BRIGHT now is available from the No.3 pin on the RGB socket which used to supply 'audio out'.

Be very careful to avoid making any connections to pins 1 and  5 as for reasons best known by Amstrad,they supply 12 volts DC.

Before putting into use, examine all connections very carefully - a blob of solder or fragment of debris bridging a connection could have very serious effects.

The monitor in use is an EGA Electishome with both analogue and TTL inputs and the +3 works very well in either mode.

X= INT((n/2!b)-2*INT((n/2!b)/2))

To clarify... Any value n can be represented in binary as noughts and ones, e.g., 7 is 00000111. Each 1 or 0 is a "bit". ### SPECTRUM +3 с TTL-монитором...

Spectrum +2 (серая модель) может работать с TTL-монитором, поскольку на разъёме RGB у него размах сигнала составляет 5 вольт (пик-пик). Однако у +3 и, предположительно, у чёрного +2a уровни сигналов RGBN соответствуют стандарту Peritel, то есть 1 вольт пик-пик, и они не могут работать со стандартным TTL- или аналоговым монитором.

Доработать +3 (issue 2), чтобы получить подходящий выходной сигнал TTL-уровня, довольно просто, если у вас есть некоторый опыт в электронике и правильные инструменты. Пригодятся хорошее зрение и увеличительное стекло. Вам понадобятся паяльник с тонким жалом и оловоотсос, а также очень полезны медицинские зажимы (артериальные щипцы).

Выкрутите винты из нижней части и сбоку корпуса +3, запоминая их расположение. Приподнимите клавиатуру и аккуратно отсоедините её шлейфы, а также светодиодный индикатор. Уберите клавиатуру в безопасное место.

Пометьте штрихом TIPPEX разъёмы дисковода и снимите его, обращая внимание на винты, после чего отложите дисковод к клавиатуре.

Выкрутите винты, крепящие основную плату к корпусу. Сейчас самое время почистить контакты разъёма расширения и другие разъёмы — чернильный ластик или ювелирная стекловолоконная кисть подойдут идеально.

Также подумайте о том, чтобы вывести наружу подключение для прямого вывода звука, используя подписанные площадки на печатной плате, к которым подключается магнитофон в модели +2a — звук отсюда намного лучше, чем со «стерео»-разъёма, предложенного Amstrad. Входной разъём тоже может оказаться полезным.

Изучите печатную плату за RGB-разъемом — компоненты на ней обозначены. Выпаяйте и удалите R35, R36, R37, R33, R31, R42 (все на 150 Ом). Замените их на резисторы 68 Ом 1/3 Вт. Эта модификация даст 8 цветов, но без «BRIGHT» (яркости).

На обратной стороне платы разорвите тонкую дорожку между R42 и R43. Удалите R42 и установите на его место сигнальный диод:
```text
>--[__]]-- конец к RGB разъему.
```

Возьмите тонкий изолированный провод и припаяйте к -[__]]- (левый конец, как показано здесь — подальше от полоски) нового диода.

Аккуратно припаяйте другой конец провода к концу диода D28 -[[__]-, отмеченному полоской на плате.

Удалите R41 (150 Ом) и R34 (470 Ом) и поменяйте их местами: R41 теперь 470 Ом, а R34 теперь 150 Ом.

BRIGHT теперь доступен на контакте №3 RGB-разъема, который раньше использовался для вывода звука («audio out»).

### Brian Cavers — всем

Несколько номеров назад я поместил письмо о проверке битов из Бейсика. Пример, который я тогда привел, был слишком специфичным, и когда мне понадобилось провести еще один похожий тест, я зашел в тупик. Поэтому я снова обратился к Chris и Paul Oliver и вывел следующую универсальную формулу для проверки того, установлен конкретный бит или нет:

```text
X= INT((n/2!b)-2*INT((n/2!b)/2))
```

где...

 n — проверяемое значение  
 b — проверяемый бит  
 ! — символ стрелки вверх (здесь его не напечатать!)

Поясню подробнее... Любое значение n можно представить в двоичном виде в виде нулей и единиц, например, 7 — это 00000111. Каждая 1 или 0 — это «бит». Компьютеры часто используют число не только (или не столько) для обозначения целой величины, сколько для хранения до восьми различных значений — по одному на каждый бит, хотя каждое из них может быть только 0 или 1. Это экономит память в тех случаях, когда информация простая, например, CAPS LOCK, который может быть только включен (1) или выключен (0). Восемь битов обычно нумеруются от 7 до 0 слева направо, поэтому, чтобы проверить, скажем, левый бит в PEEK 32768, вы должны задать `LET b=7` и `n=PEEK 32768` в приведенной выше формуле, и X примет значение 0 или 1. На этом урок окончен.
